correctness.rationale: Projection of uniform measure on each adjacent side gives constant densities on two complementary intervals divided by a perpendicular foot, forcing p_i cos A_i/ell_i constant. The converse satisfies the full stationarity identity. Two-step products of line-direction orthogonal projectors have squared operator norm 1 or cos² of intersecting angles, giving strict expected W2 contraction. Pairwise differing indices infinitely often imply all-moment uniqueness by bounded-Lipschitz convergence. Independent exact geometry calculations verified all side-balance equations for three acute triangles with p=(3/16,1/16,3/4), (1/5,2/15,2/3), (7/32,7/32,9/16). Tests corroborate, they do not replace measure-level proof.

Zeng et al. use adaptive-step Kaczmarz, Li–Wu augmented methods. The additional non-implied result is the explicit unique sidewise-uniform law on acute three-line inconsistent problems. A distinct Resultary farthest-projection map has different transition mechanics. Unread older Butnariu projection literature presents residual priority risk.

final_claim: For any nondegenerate acute triangle and iid positive frequencies p_i, random projections onto its three complete supporting lines have a unique invariant probability. It is conditionally uniform on every side iff p_i is proportional to ell_i/cos(A_i); perimeter-uniform iff equilateral. Two-step synchronous coupling gives explicit W2 contraction q_2(p)<1.
limitations: Butnariu and collaborators’ 1995 random projection invariant-measure literature was not materially read; an equivalent geometric balance law may exist.
The contraction factor q_2 is sufficient, not proved optimal, and no right/obtuse triangle claim is made.
